claims.text: You can use `pulumi import` to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.

The `pulumi import` CLI command accepts a resource type/name syntax like `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`, `pulumi import aws:ec2/subnet:Subnet private-subnet-1 subnet-67890`, and `pulumi import aws:ecs/cluster:Cluster app-cluster my-cluster`.
The `@pulumi/policy` package exports a `PolicyPack` class and a `validateResourceOfType` function.
The Pulumi Automation API is available for import from `@pulumi/pulumi/automation`.
The Pulumi Automation API's `LocalWorkspace` class exposes a `createOrSelectStack` method.
Pulumi's `pulumi.ComponentResource` class can be extended to create custom reusable component resources.
Pulumi component resources call `this.registerOutputs()` to register their outputs.

The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide teaches readers to reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi, use any Terraform provider in Pulumi programs, import and use Terraform modules directly, convert HCL code to Pulumi when beneficial, and orchestrate both Terraform and Pulumi deployments together.
Component resources can integrate with Terraform behind the scenes, hiding multi-tool management complexity from development teams while leaving it to the platform team.
